correctness.rationale: A shattered depth-d tree exists exactly when some comparison leaves two depth-(d-1) shattered version spaces; each branch must have at least 2^(d-1) orders. I tested this recurrence independently using complete comparison-sign patterns filtered by the queried sign constraints. The 2,520-order branch for 1<2 passed depth 10 and failed depth 11; all pairs and both outcomes at the unrestricted root are isomorphic by relabeling, so the unrestricted dimension is 11. For n=1 through 6 the independent search reached 0,1,2,4,6,9, and the cardinality bound certifies the respective upper bounds. Routing each permutation separately through the attached tree, with outcome 0 first, reached all 2,048 leaves with minimum occupancy 1. Replay: python3 /workspace/branches/audit_comparison.py with the frozen permutation_comparison_witness.json path as its argument. The check says nothing about ranks beyond seven.
